entity_verdicts.reasons: Existence, location, and investment figures are documented by a Tier 1 county government page and a Tier 2 SoftBank release, both confirmed verbatim (re-fetched 2026-09-27/28). Status 'planned' is appropriately conservative and does not overstate. Flag for currency: multiple news outlets (Forbes, ABQ Journal, KRWG, Energy News Beat -- all Tier 3) reported on 2026-09-24 that Oracle sent a force-majeure notice to developer STACK Infrastructure over a delayed gas-pipeline permit, expecting roughly a one-year delay. I checked SEC EDGAR full-text search for any Oracle or STACK/Blue Owl 8-K referencing 'Project Jupiter' + 'force majeure' (none found as of 2026-09-28) and re-fetched the Doña Ana County page directly (no update, no mention of the notice). No Tier 1/2 primary document yet confirms or quantifies this development, so no correction is made to status or timeline -- doing so on Tier 3 alone would violate the evidence standard. The analyst's gaps[] entry ('Project Jupiter force majeure / current status') is honest and should remain; the site's future should be treated as materially uncertain by any downstream reader.

Existence, tenant (OpenAI/Oracle), investment ($15B+), and 'close to a gigawatt' capacity are confirmed verbatim from Vantage's own Tier 2 release. Status is corrected: the Oct 2025 release said only 'construction will begin soon,' which the research file recorded as status='announced'. I found that construction has since begun -- the City of Port Washington's official project information site (portdatacenter.com, a municipal government page, i.e. Tier 1 gov_press_release-equivalent) states 'construction began in December 2025,' and Vantage's own blog has since posted community-investment and hiring/career-expo updates (March 2026 onward) consistent with active construction. This source was found during verification and is not part of the research file's sources[]; flagging rather than a plain 'publish' because the correcting citation sits outside the file's normal source_checks pipeline and should be added to sources[] on the next research pass.

Existence, location, tenant (Oracle, exclusively), and status all confirmed verbatim from Related Digital's and Oracle's own Tier 2 releases, both fetched directly. The June 2026 Oracle release independently confirms construction is underway, consistent with status='under_construction'.

The single evidence item (SoftBank's Sept 2025 release: 'SoftBank has broken ground... on track to be operational next year') is verbatim-confirmed and, read alone, supports status='under_construction'. Material flag: this is now a 12+ month-old Tier 2 source, and subsequent Tier 3 reporting (DataCenterDynamics: 'Data centers now banned in Lordstown, Ohio'; Spectrum News 1; Business Journal Daily) describes a Village Council permitting moratorium enacted Jan 2026 and later reports that SoftBank/Foxconn pivoted the site toward manufacturing modular data-center components rather than operating a data center on-site, with litigation over the ban pending before the Ohio Supreme Court. I could not find any Tier 1/2 document (a village ordinance text, a court filing, or a SoftBank statement) that would let me confidently correct the status field one way or the other, so per the 'unknown is an answer' rule I am not changing status on Tier 3 sourcing alone. The analyst's own gaps[] entry ('Lordstown, Ohio status') is honest and appropriate. Flagging this entity so the UI shows a visible caveat: the current 'under_construction' status is stale and contested, and the site's continued use as a data center is now in doubt.

Existence, tenant (OpenAI), and status ('under construction') all confirmed verbatim against the SB Energy S-1/A (fetched via r.jina.ai reader after direct SEC fetch was blocked) and SB Energy's own Tier 2 release. S-1/A table confirms Building 1 = 308 MW-IT, Building 2 = 445 MW-IT, both with 2028 RFS dates, consistent with the capacity note.

Existence, tenant (OpenAI), and the specific figures the analyst was asked to double-check -- '17 leases' signed 2026-08-17 and '8.0 GW-IT' of contracted capacity -- are all confirmed verbatim against the SB Energy S-1/A. Status='planned' is directly supported: the S-1/A states 'No data center capacity is currently in operation' and that, as of the prospectus date, PORTS-Pike has an executed lease but 'is not yet under construction.'

Existence, location, and the ~100,000 H100 / ~130MW first-cluster figures are confirmed verbatim against the SpaceX S-1/A (via SEC full-text-search exact-phrase match against this specific accession) and the MLGW utility PDF (via pdftotext). Capacity is honestly labeled as grid electric service (150MW, requesting 300MW total), distinct from the S-1/A's compute-power figures, and the note makes this distinction explicit.

Existence, location, and all cited figures (110,000 GB200/~210MW first cluster, 110,000 GB300/~220MW second cluster, Anthropic Cloud Services Agreement) confirmed verbatim against the SpaceX S-1/A via SEC full-text-search exact-phrase match. Prose audit: capacity.note additionally claimed 'S-1/A also expects a next phase of 220,000+ GB300 and 400+ additional MW' -- this specific forward-looking figure is not supported by any cited evidence. Direct fetch of the S-1/A exhibit and two sibling FWP filings that share its disclosure text (spacexukfwp.htm, japanfwp_06042026.htm, eu_interviewtranscript06.htm) turned up no sentence stating a next-phase GB300 count or additional-MW figure; EDGAR full-text search confirms '220,000' and '400+ additional megawatts' occur somewhere in the filing family but not adjacent to GB300/next-phase language in any retrievable passage, and a plain doubling of the two already-disclosed clusters (110,000+110,000=220,000; ~210+220 MW rounds toward 400+) suggests this may be an extrapolation rather than a disclosed figure. Corrected capacity.note to remove the unconfirmed sentence; downgraded to publish_flagged since the two documented clusters (confirmed) remain solid but this one forward-looking clause could not be substantiated after real effort.

summary:
Reviewed all 42 sources, 22 companies, 32 facilities, and 26 flows in the datacenter layer. Fetched every source directly (SEC filings via r.jina.ai reader proxy and EDGAR full-text-search exact-phrase matching after sec.gov blocked scripted fetches even with a descriptive User-Agent per the SEC's bot policy; all other sources via direct fetch).
